coordinates.locator: OSM building footprint centroid for 筑波実験棟 (Tsukuba experimental hall); the SuperKEKB NIM A paper names Tsukuba as the interaction-region straight section
coordinates.note: Corroboration: the OSM Tsukuba hall footprint centroid lies 4.8 m from the previous uncited value, so the coordinate is kept and its sourcing upgraded from uncertain to approximate. Previous record: detector point 36.15778, 140.075 at 400 m precision, sources ['src:superkekb-project-site']; moved 4 m (2026-09-21). The official SuperKEKB project site (previously the sole source) still backs the Tsukuba interaction-region location; the OSM footprint refines it by 4.8 m.

name: KEK Tsukuba interaction region (Belle II)
notes: Depth below the surface is not recorded: the SuperKEKB ring is commonly described as roughly 11 m underground, but no official page consulted states this.

summary.plain: The collision hall on the KEK laboratory campus in Tsukuba, Japan, where the electron and positron beams of the KEKB and SuperKEKB rings are brought together and where the Belle and Belle II detectors have stood.
summary.technical: The Tsukuba straight section of the KEKB/SuperKEKB double-ring collider, housing the interaction point and final-focus system; home of the Belle detector (1999-2010) and, after the roll-in of 11 April 2017, of Belle II.
